title: Codon usage bias in E. coli
summary: Synonymous codons are used unequally, and most unequally in highly expressed genes: translational selection on top of mutation bias.

concepts.label: Genetic code
concepts.description: The mapping of 64 codons onto 20 amino acids and stop, read here from DNA and protein side by side.

facts.text: 61 sense codons code for 20 amino acids; 3 are stops.

children.label: Codon
children.description: Three bases of a coding sequence.

children.label: Synonymous codon
children.description: Codons that code for the same amino acid; how many there are is the degeneracy.

children.label: Amino acid
children.description: What a sense codon codes for.

facts.text: Highly expressed E. coli genes prefer codons read by abundant tRNAs (Ikemura 1981).

children.label: Relative synonymous codon usage (RSCU)
children.description: A codon's count over its count if all synonyms were used equally.

children.label: Effective number of codons (Nc)
children.description: Wright's Nc, from 20 (one codon per amino acid) to 61 (no bias).

facts.text: Nc and its expected value under GC3 bias alone: Wright 1990.

children.label: GC3s
children.description: G+C share at synonymous third positions: the mark of mutation bias.

concepts.label: Gene expression level
concepts.description: How much protein a gene makes. Here only a proxy: ribosomal proteins (high) against transcription regulators (low).

children.label: Protein abundance
children.description: Measured copies per cell (PaxDb, proteomics): would replace the proxy.

concepts.label: Translational selection
concepts.description: Selection for codons that are translated fast and accurately, strongest in the most-made proteins.

children.label: tRNA gene copy number
children.description: How many tRNA genes read each codon: the supply side of codon preference.

concepts.label: Mutation bias
concepts.description: Unequal mutation rates toward G+C or A+T: sets codon usage where selection is weak.
